correctness.rationale: For singleton first-choice approval and three uniformly ranked candidates, the four exhaustive blocking tests a>0, 2a>=n, 3b<=a, 3(b+r)<=2a, 3(b+s)<=2a follow by classifying disapprover coalitions by common better rivals. Two candidate survivors would each need n/2 top votes and each be blocked by the other half. The type distribution is Multinomial(n;1/3,1/3,1/6,1/6). Exponential Markov bound using (3/2)^a(1/2)^b and the feasible type (3m,m,m,m) establish -log(27/16)/6 for all residues. The tilted mode (1/2,1/6,1/6,1/6), summable cone over h,j,ell and Stirling give the n≡0 mod6 prefactor. Independent direct strict-coalition enumeration for 27,990 candidate/profile tests through n=5 agreed; the explicit cone sum truncated at h=90 agreed with 14904/121 to 0.00031. No finite test purports to prove the n→∞ asymptotic.
